newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares plunge at close led by properties.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares plunge at close led by properties.

text.p: Singapore shares plunged in late trading on Friday, led by tumbling property stocks.
Dealers said the shares dived on rumours the government was to announce sweeping changes to the public housing market, including higher interest rates for loans.
A government spokeswoman declined comment, but said National Development Minister Lim Hng Kiang would hold a news conference on Saturday. She refused to say what it would address.
A dealer said such new property market measures, if imposed, would be another dampener on an already weak stock market. "It is like rubbing salt into the wound," he said.

Property stocks like City Developments, Wing Tai and DBS Land, dived to new year lows in active trading in the half hour before the market closed. The SES property index closed off its lows but was still down 5.06 percent at 682.19.
The key Straits Times Industrial index also closed sharply lower at 2,068.48, down 18.79 points. Total market volume was 169.29 million shares with 276 losers beating 80 gainers.
Newly listed Raffles Medical Group ended at S$0.54 against its initial offer price of S$0.38. Gainers included Singapore Press foreign, Want Want and UOB foreign.
